skill.name: vibe-security
skill.description: Security analysis skill for finding common code, dependency, configuration, and infrastructure vulnerabilities across multiple languages.
skill.summary: Scan code and dependencies for common security flaws and generate remediation guidance.
skill.author: 0x8506

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are vulnerability examples, scanner signatures, or documentation blocks rather than executable dangerous behavior. Real risks remain from local file modification in the auto-fix engine, dependency scanners that invoke package-manager tools, and privileged installation guidance in the skill documentation.

remediation.issue: Auto-fix can write to any user-supplied filepath.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain fixes to paths under the selected project directory, resolve symlinks, and require explicit confirmation before writing files.

remediation.issue: Dependency scanning invokes package-manager tools locally.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact commands, avoid shell execution, keep fixed argument lists, and warn users that tools may access registries or local package configuration.

remediation.issue: Setup instructions include privileged package installation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo and OS package-manager installation steps with a confirmation-required prerequisite check and link users to official installation documentation.

content.user_title: Audit Code Security with Vibe Security
content.value_statement: Security reviews are hard to run consistently across languages and frameworks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through vulnerability scanning, dependency checks, fix suggestions, and report generation.
actual_capabilities: Runs AST-based checks for Python code and heuristic checks for JavaScript and TypeScript.
Tracks tainted data from common user-input sources to dangerous sinks.
Searches bundled vulnerability, rule, framework, and remediation reference data.
Checks npm, Python, Go, and Rust dependencies through local audit tools when available.
Suggests remediation patterns and can apply line-level fixes with rollback support.
Generates HTML, SARIF, CSV, and JSON reports from scan results.
limitations: Results depend on bundled patterns and may miss vulnerabilities outside supported languages or frameworks.
Dependency scans require local package-manager audit tools to be installed and usable.
Auto-fix operations can change files and should be reviewed before use.
The skill is not a replacement for expert security review or penetration testing.

use_cases.title: Review application code before release
use_cases.description: Scan source files for injection, XSS, weak crypto, authentication, and unsafe deserialization patterns before deployment.

use_cases.title: Improve developer remediation speed
use_cases.description: Use fix suggestions and rollback support to help developers understand and safely correct common vulnerabilities.

use_cases.title: Prepare CI security artifacts
use_cases.description: Generate SARIF, JSON, CSV, or HTML outputs that can support code scanning workflows and audit records.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic security scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of a project directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Vibe Security to scan this project for common security vulnerabilities. Summarize critical and high findings first.

prompt_templates.title: Check one file for injection risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a changed source file
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this file with Vibe Security for SQL injection, command injection, XSS, and unsafe deserialization. Explain each confirmed issue.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest safe remediations
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer needs fixes for known findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Vibe Security to propose fixes for these vulnerabilities. Include safer patterns, tests to run, and any behavior changes to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a release security report
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full Vibe Security review for code, dependencies, and configuration. Generate a prioritized report with remediation owners and release blockers.

output_examples.input: Scan my Express API before release.
output: Critical issues are listed first with affected files and recommended fixes.
Dependency findings are separated from source-code findings.
The summary includes follow-up tests for authentication, injection, and XSS paths.

output_examples.input: Review this Python handler for command injection.
output: The report identifies unsafe command construction when user input reaches process execution.
It recommends argument arrays, strict allowlists, and tests for rejected inputs.

output_examples.input: Generate an audit report for CI results.
output: The skill can format scan results into readable summaries and machine-consumable artifacts.
The output separates severity, vulnerability type, affected location, and remediation guidance.

best_practices: Run scans on a clean branch and review any auto-fix diff before committing changes.
Install and verify local audit tools before relying on dependency scan results.
Treat scanner findings as triage input and confirm exploitability in application context.
anti_patterns: Do not run auto-fix on sensitive repositories without reviewing target paths and backups.
Do not ignore high-severity findings just because they appear in generated reports.
Do not treat bundled examples as proof that the target application is vulnerable.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Some workflows invoke local audit tools such as npm audit, pip-audit, go list, and cargo audit.

faq.question: Can it modify my files?
faq.answer: Yes. The auto-fix engine can write changes and create backups. Review changes before accepting them.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The documentation covers JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, PHP, Java, Go, and Ruby, with strongest script support for Python and JavaScript.

faq.question: Does it find dependency vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It can call local audit tools for npm, Python, Go, and Rust projects when those tools and manifest files are present.

faq.question: Can it generate reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes report generation for HTML, SARIF, CSV, and JSON formats from scan result data.

faq.question: Is this enough for compliance?
faq.answer: No. It can support evidence gathering, but compliance decisions need human review and organization-specific controls.
